testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

survived.evidence: grep -n -- '-\*) ;;' agent-test tests/agent-test.test.mjs returned only tests/agent-test.test.mjs:1482. agent-test:646-651 holds the new multi-line `-*)` arm.

That comment says the flag-detection arm is `-*) ;;`. agent-test:646-651 now has a multi-line `-*)` arm with an `if [ -n "$operand" ]` refusal body. The pr.diff line 10 removes `-*) ;;` and line 23 adds `-*)`. The comment is stale, though minor, since its narrowing-to-`--*` argument still holds. unverified.claim: The comment at agent-test:~109 says 'the flag arm names nothing and stays silent'. The flag arm can now refuse with exit 1 and a message, so 'stays silent' is stale. The comment at ~120-123 ('each of the nine exits inside this loop is `exit 1`') is also unchecked against the new tenth exit, and the new arm is itself an exit that reads $operand.
unverified.evidence: agent-test:105-109 and 120-123 are untouched by the diff. The new refusal at agent-test:646-651 prints to stderr and exits 1 inside the loop. A grep of non-comment lines in 102-738 found 13 lines containing `exit 1`, so the 'nine' figure cannot be tied to a count in the current tree.
unverified.suggested_fix: Say the flag arm records no operand, and either recount the exits or drop the number.

unverified.claim: PR body: '`--import=./setup.mjs` keeps working' is true only when the flag comes before the first path. After a path, the new arm refuses every dash-led non-existent argument, `=` form included.
unverified.evidence: agent-test:646-651 refuses any `-*` argument that is not an existing path whenever $operand is non-empty. It does not look at whether the flag has an `=`.
unverified.suggested_fix: State 'before the first path' in the body.

unverified.claim: The new test's last check, `const dashes = a.run("--", "t/a.test.mjs"); assert.equal(dashes.status, 0, …)`, repeats the `"--"` row of the existing test "a node --test flag reaches node instead of being read as a path" (test:1458-1461), which runs the same argv `a.run("--", "t/a.test.mjs")` and makes the same exit-0 check. It adds a runner spawn and catches no defect the older test misses.
unverified.evidence: In my copy I added a mutant to the `-*)` arm that refuses `--` only before any operand: `[ -z "$operand" ] && [ "$arg" = -- ] && { echo MUTANT >&2; exit 1; }`. Then I ran `node --test --test-reporter=spec --test-name-pattern=flag tests/agent-test.test.mjs`. Result: `✖ runner: a node --test flag reaches node instead of being read as a path` (`AssertionError: --: MUTANT`), `✖ runner: an argv of flags alone refuses…`, and `✖ runner: a flag after a test path is refused…` (`AssertionError: MUTANT`, failing only at the `dashes` assertion, since the loop rows and the `dash` row carry other messages). So the older test already catches what `dashes` guards. With the mutant reverted and the `dashes` lines deleted, the same command printed `ℹ tests 3 ℹ pass 3 ℹ fail 0`.
unverified.suggested_fix: Delete lines 1564-1565 (`const dashes = …` and its `assert.equal`). Optionally add a comment pointing to the existing `--`-before-file row in the earlier test.

unverified.claim: The `dash` block recomputes `dash.stdout + dash.stderr` four times across three assertions. The loop just above already binds that once as `out`.
unverified.evidence: In my copy I replaced lines 1559-1562 with `const dash = a.run("t/a.test.mjs", "-dash.test.mjs"); const dashOut = dash.stdout + dash.stderr; assert.notEqual(dash.status, 0, dashOut); assert.match(dashOut, /node: bad option/, dashOut); assert.doesNotMatch(dash.stderr, /agent-test: /, dashOut);`. Then I ran `node --test --test-reporter=spec --test-name-pattern=flag tests/agent-test.test.mjs`: `✔ runner: a flag after a test path is refused, not silently dropped by node`, `ℹ tests 3 ℹ pass 3 ℹ fail 0`. The assertions check the same values as before.
unverified.suggested_fix: `const dashOut = dash.stdout + dash.stderr;` and use `dashOut` for the match target and the three messages. `doesNotMatch` keeps reading `dash.stderr` alone.
